items.stem: In Svelte, you call items.push(x) on an array bound in the template, but the view does not update. Why?

options.text: Svelte reactivity triggers on assignment, not on in-place mutation
options.rationale: Correct: reassign (items = [...items, x]) or assign items = items to signal the change.

options.text: Arrays cannot be reactive in Svelte
push is not a valid array method
options.rationale: push is valid; it just does not trigger Svelte's reactivity.

options.text: The component must be wrapped in a store
options.rationale: A store is not required; an assignment suffices.

items.explanation: Correct: reassign (items = [...items, x]) or assign items = items to signal the change.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about SvelteKit load functions are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A +page.server.js load runs only on the server
options.rationale: Correct: server load functions never ship to the client.

options.text: A universal +page.js load can run on both server and client
options.rationale: Correct: universal loads run in both environments.

options.text: Secrets in a universal load are safe because they never reach the browser
options.rationale: Universal loads run on the client too, so secrets would leak.

options.text: load functions cannot return data to the page
options.rationale: Returning data to the page is their primary purpose.

items.explanation: Correct: server load functions never ship to the client.

items.stem: A route is prerendered at build time. Which operation will NOT work on that page?

options.text: Reading a per-request cookie to personalise content
options.rationale: Correct: prerendered output is built once with no request context, so per-request cookies are unavailable.
Static content is exactly what prerendering is for.
Build-time data is available during prerendering.
Links work fine on prerendered pages.
